basis: Ushojo baale hair matches vā́la and Shina baal, with a final e cell and initial stress. The ending must be identified before using it as an unextended noun comparison.

Brokskat hat and Ushojo hʌt hand preserve h/t of hásta after cluster simplification. Both are short unmarked monosyllables, so they are segmental controls but have no observed early/late mora contrast.

Brokskat diṭ handspan matches the diṣṭi/dist handspan set through reduction of the medial cluster. diṣṭi versus the competing vitasti tradition remains a historical etymological question, not an accent-selected choice.
Ushojo sʌ he matches the inherited sá demonstrative/pronominal base, without a marked accent in this survey token.

Brokskat ṣiṣ and Ushojo ṣuṣ head preserve the sibilant frame of śīrṣá and directly match the short Shinaic head set. Shortening removes the long-vowel mora contrast; absent marks are not tonelessness.
Ushojo ṣuna hear preserves the śru/śr̥ṇ present-root nasal and has initial syllable stress; its imperative/citation ending differs from the Sanskrit finite headword.
Brokskat kon this hear is an ear-plus-do expression: kon matches kárṇa ear. It is a compound/component comparison, not a reflex of śr̥ṇoti; the auxiliary requires separate analysis.

Brokskat hɨɨ and Ushojo hilo heart match the contracted hr̥daya/hi(yo)/hilo set. Ushojo's l and final o indicate a formation history beyond direct loss of the old medial consonants; initial syllable stress alone does not identify mora.

Ushojo ugoro heavy has the independently segmentable u(d)-guru formation, matching Sawi ugəro and preserving the added initial syllable. Medial stress belongs to the root-final adjective pattern, not old guru alone.
Ushojo khuni heel matches the khuriṇī/khunike heel formation with n retained. This favors the extended hoof noun over unextended khura, independently of its initial stress.

Ushojo meaṣi honey and maṣuli honeybee share the mākṣiká bee/honey base. The bee has additional ul/i morphology and final stress; it must not be pooled with the shorter honey formation. Unequal ea is not automatically a single long vowel.
Brokskat ṣiṅ horn and Ushojo ṣiŋge horns match śŕ̥ṅga, with Ushojo plural e and initial stress. Brokskat's acute is treated only as stress pending the printed cell, not inherited mora accent.

Brokskat aays and Ushojo ašpi/ašpo horse belong to áśva. Ushojo's gender pair independently reveals final i/o endings and root stress; Brokskat's unusual aay sequence requires source reading and cannot be treated as ordinary aa.

Brokskat hot and Ushojo tato match taptá with pt simplification and final o. Ushojo initial short syllable stress is explicit. The DB Brokskat taáto may contain a neighboring-column accent, so its exact printed reading is pending; no mora claim is licensed for Brokskat regardless.

Brokskat gooṭ and Ushojo gooṭ house match gōṣṭhá with preserved retroflex stop, which independently distinguishes this family from ghōṣa/goṣ. Unmarked long Ushojo oo supplies quantity but not a mora location.
Ushojo kʌcaak how many directly matches Shina kʌcaak in the kiyatta quantity-interrogative family; final stress and aa are explicit. The extra k formation must be retained in historical comparison.
Brokskat šo hundred matches śatá with intervocalic t loss and contraction; no accent is marked.
Brokskat mõ and Ushojo mʌ/mɑ̃ I match the first-person ma/oblique-derived pronoun family. These are grammatical remodeling evidence, not a direct continuation of nominative ahám accent.
Brokskat giab irrigation channel plausibly matches yavyā/yab with a palatal onset spelling. It has no marked stress and requires exact source interpretation of gia before quantity coding.

Brokskat maris kill has the causative mār killing root plus recurring is citation morphology. Final stress belongs to that modern citation formation and does not directly reproduce the old finite suffix sequence.

Ushojo goṇ knot matches granthí through the independently attested gŭṇ knot set. Old medial cluster reduction and vowel rounding are shared; its unmarked short nucleus is not informative about mora accent.

Ushojo uran lamb directly matches úraṇa ram/lamb but stresses the second syllable. This is a real syllable-shift candidate in an unextended disyllabic kin/animal noun, requiring quantity/formation comparison rather than preservation by default.
Ushojo khuṭo lame/dwarf agrees exactly with Palula khuṭo in the khōra/khōṭa lame family. Initial root stress is explicit; the final o is an adjective ending.

Brokskat haazis and Ushojo haasi laugh match hásati, with voicing of the Brokskat s and citation morphology. Both retain initial syllable stress in the actual modern forms; root length history is a separate question.

Brokskat pannii leaf retains the nasal of parṇá, unlike páttra-derived paṭo. Its final stress is an independently motivated nasal-stem/feminine-i comparison and must not be counted as an exception to the paṭo adjective-like formation.
Ushojo paṭo leaf preserves the retroflex stop expected in the páttra set, with final o; the survey token itself lacks an accent mark.

Ushojo laoko light matches laghú plus extension and Shina laoko. Stress on the second written vowel group is explicit; hiatus versus diphthong cannot be silently collapsed, making this useful evidence for the precontraction structure behind lhooku-type forms.
Ushojo truṭo lip matches Shina trūṭi in the tuṇḍa snout/lip family with metathesis and an extended final vowel. Initial stress is clear, but the metathesis/quantity chronology remains open.

Brokskat gim liver plausibly belongs with Shina yum/yūm and yákr̥t. The initial palatal/velar and final m require the same substantial inherited remodeling already present in the Shina family; no independent Brokskat accent is marked.

Brokskat ẓigo and Ushojo ẓugo long preserve the characteristic affricated/retroflex onset and g of dīrghá; both have initial syllable stress and final o. Their root quantity is not the old long ī unchanged.
Brokskat ẓwaa and Ushojo jũ louse match yū́kā with palatal onset and k loss, though Brokskat waa needs phonological interpretation. These short/sequence forms carry no independent mora reading.

Brokskat lic-aa nit preserves l plus affricate of likṣā́ and has final stress. The printed apostrophe position and possible two-syllable realization need verification before assuming that c-aa is one nucleus.
Ushojo phʌph lung matches the phupphusa/phāpu expressive lung family, retaining reduplicated labials, not vákṣas or bhaṣma. No accent is marked.
